title: List Variables Basics
description: MENTOR-9: "Sometimes one value isn't enough. We need to store multiple related items—like all damaged systems, or all crew members. That's where list variables come in."

theory.title: List Variables: Managing Collections
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 displays a holographic array of system statuses, each floating in its own compartment.

MENTOR-9: "See these? Five separate systems. We could create five variables, but that's messy. Instead, we use a LIST—one variable holding multiple values, indexed numerically."

What Are List Variables?

A list variable stores multiple values in a specific order, like a numbered container with slots:

@{systems}    Create List    Nav    Shields    Engines
# Now @{systems} contains 3 items at indices 0, 1, 2

List Syntax

  • Declare/create: @{list_name}
  • Access entire list: @{list_name}
  • Access single item: ${list_name}[index]

Note the syntax difference:

  • @{} = entire list (multiple values)
  • ${} = single item from list (one value)

Creating Lists

Use the Create List keyword:

@{colors}    Create List    red    green    blue
@{numbers}    Create List    10    20    30    40
@{empty}    Create List    # Empty list

Accessing List Items by Index

Lists are zero-indexed (first item is at position 0):

@{items}    Create List    A    B    C    D
Log    ${items}[0]    # Output: A (first)
Log    ${items}[1]    # Output: B (second)
Log    ${items}[2]    # Output: C (third)
Log    ${items}[3]    # Output: D (fourth)

Negative Indices

Use negative numbers to count from the end:

@{items}    Create List    A    B    C    D
Log    ${items}[-1]    # Output: D (last)
Log    ${items}[-2]    # Output: C (second-to-last)

Adding Items to Lists

Use Append To List to add items at the end:

@{systems}    Create List    Nav    Shields
Append To List    ${systems}    Engines
# Now @{systems} = [Nav, Shields, Engines]

Important: When modifying a list, use ${list} not @{list}:

  • ✅ Append To List ${systems} Engines
  • ❌ Append To List @{systems} Engines

Logging Lists

Two ways to log lists:

@{systems}    Create List    A    B    C

# Log entire list as comma-separated
Log    All systems: @{systems}
# Output: All systems: A, B, C

# Log entire list as Python list representation
Log    ${systems}
# Output: ['A', 'B', 'C']

Common List Operations

  • Create List: Make a new list
  • Append To List: Add item to end
  • Get Length: Count items in list
  • Get From List: Get item at index (alternative to ${list}[index])
  • Set List Value: Change item at specific index
  • Remove From List: Delete item at index
  • Insert Into List: Add item at specific position

Why Use Lists?

  • Group related data: All system names in one variable
  • Iterate easily: Process each item in a loop (covered later)
  • Dynamic data: Add/remove items as needed
  • Ordered storage: Items maintain their position

Real-World Example

*** Test Cases ***
Browser Testing
    @{browsers}    Create List    chrome    firefox    edge
    FOR    ${browser}    IN    @{browsers}
        Open Browser    ${URL}    ${browser}
        Run Tests
        Close Browser
    END

This loops through all browsers and runs tests on each one—powerful!
